title: 本地阅读器 T0–T5 功能合同

T0-rar-cbr.output: read-only archive entries using the existing ArchiveReader chapter/page model
acceptance: corrupt, encrypted, unsupported RAR variants report a reason
constraints: use Junrar for read-only extraction; the project must not implement RAR-compatible archive creation
single-volume unencrypted RAR/CBR is the initial supported scope
reopen and rescan the SAF stream for requested pages; do not create temporary archive or page files

T1-bookmarks.output: multiple persistent bookmark entries per comic, newest first
constraints: removing a comic removes its bookmarks

T2-auto-next.input: end-of-chapter event and global reader preference
T2-auto-next.output: opens next chapter at page zero only when enabled and a next chapter exists
constraints: last chapter remains at its last page

T3-duplicates.input: indexed comic title and archive size
T3-duplicates.output: user-confirmed duplicate candidates grouped by case-insensitive title plus exact byte size
constraints: removal only drops local library references

T4-backup.input: versioned JSON backup selected via SAF
T4-backup.output: export/import of app-owned progress, bookmarks, reader settings, tags, favorites, booklists, and history
constraints: validate schema/version and all entries before applying
exclude comics, SAF grants, derived cover cache, and device-only UI state
restore keyed user state only when comic IDs remain stable; SAF URI identity may differ on another device
invalid input leaves current state unchanged

T5-webtoon.input: vertical scroll mode and current chapter page list
T5-webtoon.output: lazy page rendering with bounded decoded image residency and restoration to saved page
constraints: restore the saved page on comic/chapter entry without fighting live scroll updates

error_behavior: unsupported archive details are surfaced to the user
backup parse errors do not mutate stores
duplicate cleanup never removes source documents
verification: unit tests for archive classification, bookmark persistence, merge validation, duplicate grouping, and scroll-position mapping
manual device check for chapter transition and long-strip memory behavior
